inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin is pointing to more housing tenancies while the number of people in emergency accommodation has increased again and eviction notices are causing concern. That is no success story: a government can boast about leases, but families need homes they can actually keep. Forcing landlords to provide six-year leases from March 1 may sound protective, yet rules that make renting harder can leave ordinary people with fewer choices. The test is whether people have secure homes—not whether ministers can point to a headline figure.
